Sidney Lansfield, a celebrated movie director for Adolph Zucca, and who substituted in the original Dixieland Jazz Band in 1917, when Henry Ragus was ill in New Orleans for two weeks.

Here we go. It's ready. We left New Orleans for Chicago Thursday, March 2, 1916, 8.30 a.m. I arrived in Chicago Friday, March 3, 1916, about 9.30. This train was late due to a severe snowstorm. Mom said, take you overboard. Mom don't know. We couldn't be bothered with those things besides it was warm in New Orleans. We did take our new straw hats and walk down Wabash Avenue in zero temperature with them. We opened at the Schiller Cafe owned by Sam Ahern, managed by Harry James, the latter style as a jazz band, J-A-S, and so advertised in that way. One night, as the Schiller patron became so emotional, he twirled a walking cane around his head and let it fly, hitting several people in his flight, shouting, jazz are up, fellas, jazz are up. We had never heard the term used before in connection with music or a band, and seen from that time on were known as a jazz band.
I wondered if you could tell me when the drums changed there. After the Schiller Cafe.

After the Schiller. Three months in 1916, Stein was with us. He stayed on and got another band, and for I think three weeks at the Del Abbey, we had a drummer, a Chicago boy. I don't remember his name now. And then Spivaro came with us when we went to the Casino Gardens.
And your clarinet changed too, didn't it? Somewhere around there.

At the Casino Gardens later. I had a little trouble at managing the band and paying them off. They were allowed, two of them were allowed to, well we all were allowed if we wished, to sign tabs up at the bar upstairs. Naturally some of them abused it. One of them said I didn't, said he didn't owe a certain amount of money. And I was holding the bag for four dollars, which I didn't like. So I thought and devised a way of getting this money, this four dollars back. Because I didn't like losing it. There was no reason why I should pay for anyone's drinks. Particularly when they couldn't hold the liquor. So I thought of paying them in one dollar bills. And as I counted them, I counted one, two, three, four, passing a dollar bill each time. Five, passing no dollar bill. Six, passing a dollar bill on. And that way, I got two dollars out of his pay. The following week, I did the same thing. Count it right before his eyes and you put it in his pocket. I got my four dollars back. Wasn't a nice way to get it, but I was determined to get it. I didn't wish to lose it. Especially under those considerations, conditions. Max Hart came to Chicago. I wrote everybody trying to get the band to New York. Actors would come and say, oh, you want to get to New York. New York is the place. Shields didn't like New York. He had come here with Brown's band and they were a failure. And he influenced LaRocca. LaRocca wanted to stay in Chicago. Getting forty dollars a week more than he ever earned in his life. He wished to stay there. In fact, any of us have ruined our lives. He wished to stay in Chicago. But, when Max Hart was the only one who gave us anything concrete, he gave us, I think he offered us for the band, a three-week contract with an option. I don't know how many weeks. Option, I think three months, if I remember. At three hundred and fifty dollars a week for the band. Well, when the option expired, we got more money on that. We got something like five hundred and twenty-eight dollars a week.
Who was the clarinet between Shields and Nunes, if any? Was there anybody in between? Nobody?

Shields joined at, Shields had been around Chicago and he hadn't been doing anything. And we saw him. And I asked him, how would you like to come with us? Geez, I wish I could. I said, well, I think we'll be able to make it because Nunes, every once in a while, he quits. Comes in late. Quits. He thinks he can't get anyone else. And he believes that he has the upper hand. So, the next time he quits, which will be in a few days, because he does it almost nightly. He will call you up and you come right down. So, he did. And Shields was with us then on. That was about, at the Casino Gardens around, and then on. It was early summer. June of July, 1916. So, March, April, May, June. Yes. June of July, 1916. July, most likely.
